title: Second-limit Čech comparison for an affine étale covering
statement:
Let $X$ be affine, $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, $F$ an étale left $\Lambda$-module sheaf, and $M=\nu_X^*F$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $L$ be a small nonempty directed set and let $U=\varprojlim_{i\in L}U_i$ with $U_i\to X$ affine étale of finite presentation and affine transitions [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Fix $i_0\in L$ and a finite affine étale covering $\{W_{a,i_0}\to U_{i_0}\}_{a=1}^m$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For $i\ge i_0$ put $W_{a,i}=W_{a,i_0}\times_{U_{i_0}}U_i$ and $W_a=W_{a,i_0}\times_{U_{i_0}}U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The section restriction maps canonically identify
$$\varinjlim_{i\ge i_0}\check C^\bullet(\{W_{a,i}\to U_i\},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\check C^\bullet(\{W_a\to U\},M)$$
and induce isomorphisms on every Čech cohomology group. The complexes are those of [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech]. This comparison assumes no injectivity or vanishing.

proof.text: Use the upper tail J = {i : L // i₀ ≤ i}. It contains i₀ and is directed. Its opposite inclusion into Lᵒᵖ is initial, by the common-upper-bound criterion. Whiskering the supplied underlying-scheme limit cone along this inclusion retains its limit. This argument does not assume a nonempty cover.

Regard each supplied SiteCechComplex tuple object as the wide pullback of its nonempty list of covering factors over the base. Its universal property supplies the limit cone. The étale-to-pro-étale inclusion preserves these finite limits; the forgetful functors to schemes preserve connected limits. Construct stage transitions and limit-to-stage maps by these universal properties and the pullback universal property. Check their identities, compositions and their commutation with all tuple deletion maps by the projections. Stage covering factors and stage tuple objects are affine because their underlying finite-limit diagrams consist of affine schemes (Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit). No new site objects or covering assertions are required: U and T are already supplied in X.ProEt.

Verify the underlying-scheme tuple cone is limiting explicitly. For a compatible cone z, its composites to the stage bases give a cone on the upper-tail base diagram, hence a unique map b to U. Its composites to each original W_a agree at all stages, using the morphism from each stage to i₀; write these maps a_k. The pullback universal property produces maps (a_k,b) to the limiting covering factors, and the tuple universal property combines them. Check all stage legs and uniqueness by the covering-factor projections and the supplied base limit. Repeated indices are separate projections.

Apply the adopted, proved theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isColimit_comparisonUpperStar_mapCocone_of_isAffine in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Comparison.Continuity to each affine tuple diagram and its underlying-scheme limiting cone. This theorem works in any Grothendieck abelian coefficient category, in particular left modules over the given possibly noncommutative ring. Precompose its section diagram by the invertible comparison-unit natural transformation (full faithfulness). The resulting cocone has legs exactly the comparison unit followed by restriction along s. Forgetting scalars preserves the filtered colimit. This directly supplies the section part of the comparison, without a coordinate-ring presentation or ind-étale-stability argument.

For each degree p the tuple index set (Fin (p+1) → Fin m) is finite, including when it is empty. The cochains form the product of their section groups, with evaluation projections. Filtered colimits in abelian groups preserve this finite product. Compare the two product cones via the coordinate colimit isomorphisms; their projection equations identify the induced map with the specified cocone leg. The product universal property therefore proves degreewise colimitingness.

Naturality of the comparison unit and the tuple deletion identities commute with each signed summand of the Čech differential. Construct the actual cochain maps and the diagram and cocone from them, checking their laws coordinatewise. Degreewise colimitingness gives the colimit in nonnegative cochain complexes. Extension by zero preserves colimits: evaluation at a nonnegative integer is naturally isomorphic to the corresponding original evaluation, and at a negative integer is zero.

Use filtered-colimit exactness in abelian groups, with universe restriction from the section universe to the small index universe. Regard a diagram of short complexes as a short complex in the functor category. The natural homology isomorphisms for evaluation and exact colimit identify its homology colimit with the homology of its colimit; their naturality verifies the cocone legs. Taking the three adjacent terms of a nonnegative cochain complex preserves colimits, and its composition with short-complex homology is naturally isomorphic to degree-q homology. Thus the homology functor preserves the constructed colimit for every q, including q=0.
